title: Placement: Inversion Count in Array
description: Given an array of integers `arr`, find the Inversion Count. Two elements `arr[i]` and `arr[j]` form an inversion if `arr[i] > arr[j]` and `i < j`.
constraints:
1 <= len(arr) <= 10^5
• Time: O(N log N) | Space: O(N)
solution:
def count_inversions(arr: list[int]) -> int:
    def merge_sort(a):
        if len(a) <= 1:
            return a, 0
        mid = len(a) // 2
        left, inv_left = merge_sort(a[:mid])
        right, inv_right = merge_sort(a[mid:])
        merged = []
        inv_count = inv_left + inv_right
        i = j = 0
        while i < len(left) and j < len(right):
            if left[i] <= right[j]:
                merged.append(left[i])
                i += 1
            else:
                merged.append(right[j])
                inv_count += len(left) - i
                j += 1
        merged.extend(left[i:])
        merged.extend(right[j:])
        return merged, inv_count
    _, count = merge_sort(arr)
    return count
explanation: Modified merge sort counts inversions during the merge step in O(N log N) time and O(N) space.
